name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default but allow users to toggle to light mode. This keeps eye strain low for long sessions while respecting individual preference—trade-off is slightly slower load times for the theme switcher. The dark theme matches our competitive analysis (Manus, Graphify) and aligns with the "dark-themed interface" pattern users expect from data-heavy tools.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk isn’t load time—it’s that a one-click toggle still assumes users know what’s best for their eyes. Better alternative: default to system preference, then let users override once with a persistent prompt. Settle this with A/B tests measuring actual session lengths and reported strain over two weeks.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default and let users override it once with a persistent prompt tied to their system preference. This cuts the trade-off of slower load times from a toggle while still respecting individual comfort—users who prefer light mode won’t hunt for a setting they’ll never use. The prompt removes the guesswork: we ask once, then trust their choice, aligning with our goal of clarity and enjoyment. The trade-off is a one-time interruption, but it’s smarter than forcing users to manually adjust every session.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Defaulting to system preference ignores users who switch themes frequently—like programmers toggling for screen glare—so the real risk is forcing them into a one-size-fits-all default. Better alternative: default to system preference, but expose a persistent, non-modal banner that lets users lock their choice without hunting for settings. Settle this with A/B tests tracking theme-switch frequency and user-reported fatigue over two weeks.
